business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Export Distribution of High-Proof Traditional Sorghum Baijiu

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 4 July 1984)

Convention between France and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 26 November 2013, effective 1 January 2014)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI, negotiated in principle on 30 December 2020, under EU ratification process)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 to L561-53, L561-55 to L561-57 and R561-1 to R561-57 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Articles L561-46 and R561-57 et seq. on the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) held at the Commercial Court registry; transposition of EU Directives 2015/849 (AMLD4) and 2018/843 (AMLD5); Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018; General Tax Code Article 1649-0 A; French Customs Code and Regulations on obligation of due diligence in the alcohol trade.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of shareholders' valid national passport (identity pages)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: People's Republic of China Public Security Bureau / Entry-Exit Administration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each foreign shareholder/director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local utility provider or licensed bank in China

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (police clearance certificate) for money laundering, drug offences, or bankruptcy
Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing (if the shareholder is an entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation of the People's Republic of China

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming existing relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank (e.g., Bank of China, ICBC, Standard Chartered China)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised articles of association and power of attorney (if the incorporation is delegated to a service provider)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notariat of the People's Republic of China

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and persons with signature authority against the consolidated list of financial sanctions maintained by the EU Council, the UN consolidated sanctions list, the French Tracfin national list (Gil), the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and the French financial intelligence unit's specific alerts. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign), for entities with ownership or intent from high-risk third countries, and for all transactions linked to sectors subject to anti-money-laundering obligations. The AML/CFT system must incorporate real-time sanctions filtering and periodic re-screening of UBOs at least every 12 months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); RCS clearance via the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce accessible through Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin characters; any foreign element (Chinese ideograms, for example) must be romanised in pinyin, with the transliteration recorded in the bylaws and on the registration form. The name must contain a reference to the corporate form 'SARL' in the statute. In application of Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Toubon law), the name and all compulsory legal documents addressed to the authorities must be in French or accompanied by a French translation; a French-language version of the name is to be used in public and commercial documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms that imply a public institution or governmental authority (e.g., 'République', 'Ministère', 'Ambassade', 'Préfecture', 'Police')
Terms reserved for regulated financial or insurance activities (e.g., 'Banque', 'Assurance', 'Courtier', 'Crédit', 'Société Fiduciaire')

Terms that are protected indications of origin under French or EU law (e.g., 'Cognac', 'Champagne', 'Bordeaux', 'Armagnac' or any reference to a protected geographical indication without authorisation)
Words that are contrary to public order or bonnes mœurs, or which mislead the public as to the actual scope and object of the company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested name is not approved, the applicant may file an administrative objection before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce (juge des référés) within one month of receipt of the refusal notification. An informal amendment and resubmission may be made without delay through the Guichet Unique. A separate civil remedy exists before the INPI in cases of conflict with a registered trademark; notice of opposition or cancellation proceedings must be filed within two months of the publication of the conflicting trademark application in the Bulletin Officiel de la Propriété Industrielle (BOPI).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office (domiciliation commerciale) is permissible for a SARL under Articles L123-11-2 and L123-11-3 of the French Commercial Code, provided the domiciliation company holds a special licence and statutory records are accessible at that address. The activity of export wholesale of alcoholic beverages does not appear in the statutory restrictions on domiciliation; however, the company must maintain a true physical presence for customs formalities, and must inform the DGDDI of the actual address where the accounting records and operational documents are held. A full administrative seat may be a virtual address, but an operational address in France is recommended for substance and for the benefit of tax residence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70% estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of activity, owing to the obligations of the French Customs and Excise (DGDDI) regarding alcohol and the sector-specific risk-based control plan of the Directorate-General for Competition Policy, Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control (DGCCRF).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and availability check via RCS/Greffe and preparation of the certificate of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (RCS registration tariff, no added fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal advertisement of the intended company formation in an official legal announcements journal (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (regulated tariff between €150 and €190)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SARL with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed regulatory fee for a standard SARL (approx. €81-120)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Issuance of the Kbis certificate and publication of the legal status
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (€1.98 per page plus online delivery charges)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and legalization/apostille of six Chinese documents (passports, address, police certificate, corporate register, bank letter, power of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Ministry of Justice soft seal and French Embassy (if requested)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (¥50 per apostille in China, €20-50 per document for consular services; includes courier)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of all non-French documents into French (standardised legal translations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (expert judiciaire accredited with the cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of €30-40 per standard page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the articles of association (statuts) and full legal incorporation advice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SARL (€1,500-€3,500, depending on complexity)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration with the French Customs and Excise Service (DGDDI) for the alcohol goods activity (statutory declaration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application for the sectoral licence/authorization for the wholesale distribution of alcoholic beverages (Loi du 19 juillet 1996)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free of charge, administrative authorization with no tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II – Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL constitution, capital, management); general rules at Articles L.210-1 to L.210-11; registration provisions at Articles L.123-1 and L.123-3; implemented by the Guichet Unique under Law No. 2020-1525
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), acting through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (Infogreffe / procedures.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire Unique de Création M0 (Déclaration de Constitution d'une Société à Responsabilité Limitée) together with signed Statuts and annexes
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for SARL under Law No. 2003-721; capital is freely set by the shareholders, must be fully paid in cash at constitution and deposited into a temporarily blocked escrow bank account in the name of the company in formation until RCS registration, per Article L.223-7 of the Commercial Code
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST CORPORATE RESOLUTION OF THE SARL. The founding shareholders, acting unanimously pursuant to Articles L.223-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, resolve: (1) the entire share capital, being EUR 10,000, is hereby subscribed and fully deposited in a blocked escrow account in the name of the Company at an approved credit institution; (2) the registered office is fixed at 25 Rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France, where legal service shall be established; (3) the appointed Gérant is hereby vested with full powers of direction, representation and signature; (4) all publication, deposit and registration formalities required for RCS incorporation are approved, ratified and authorised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Availability Verification and Preliminary Trademark Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – data.inpi.fr database and the Guichet Unique (procedures.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a comprehensive search against French company names, registered trademarks and pending applications to verify that the proposed corporate name 'FR SARL' and any associated brand can be lawfully adopted. Download and archive the no-conflict search report. Optionally reserve the name through the Guichet Unique before drafting statutes.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of founding shareholders
Certificate of name availability / no-conflict search report
Statement of proposed corporate object (ISIC 4632 wholesale distribution of alcoholic beverages)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a prior conflicting name or trademark is identified, select alternates, re-run the search and amend the corporate name before publication; file opposition if an infringing application is published.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Optional Notarisation of the Articles of Association (Statuts de la SARL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders or their legal counsel; notary (notaire) mandatory only where real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts containing the corporate form, registered office, corporate object covering wholesale export of Chinese baijiu and spirits, share capital, classes of shares, gérant appointment and powers, transfer restrictions, voting rules, audit thresholds and duration. Execute the deed either as a private deed (acte sous seing privé) with authentic signatures of all shareholders or as a notarised deed if required.
required_dossiers: Completed draft statuts and annexes
Copies of passports / national ID cards of all shareholders
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement, domiciliation contract or ownership title)
French-law power of attorney if any shareholder acts through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct omissions or legal deficiencies by an amending deed approved by the shareholders before publication; redraft entirely if a notary detects mandatory provision non-compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Share Capital and Deposit into Temporary Blocked Escrow Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved credit institution (full-service French or EU bank) or notary acting as depositary; Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations as fallback
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the SARL in formation, transfer the subscribed capital from each shareholder's account, and obtain the bank's certificate of blocked funds (attestation de dépôt des fonds) naming the subscribers, the amount and confirming that funds are unavailable except for remittance to the company upon registration.
required_dossiers: Project or signed statuts
Individual bank transfer receipts from each shareholder
AML/KYC declarations and source-of-funds statements
Completed bank onboarding forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected attestation if subscriber names or amounts are inaccurate; if the bank refuses the escrow structure, engage another institution and repeat the transfer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Publication of Formation Notice in a Legal Announcements Newspaper (Journal d'Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcements newspaper (JAL) authorised by the Préfecture within the département of the registered office (Paris)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the draft notice to the JAL containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, object summary, gérant identification and intended RCS registration; obtain the publisher's official attestation of publication (justificatif de parution) after the notice appears.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts or certified true copy
Bank certificate of blocked funds
French-language notice text
Payment order for publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the newspaper rejects or misprints the notice, correct the text and republish; seek confirmatory advice from the greffe if the legal content is challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Single Formation Declaration M0 with the Guichet Unique and RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (electronic portal procedures.gouv.fr) operated on behalf of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 declaration, upload the signed statuts, JAL publication attestation, blocked funds certificate, gérant identity and powers, registered office proof and regulated activity declarations. Pay the greffe fee electronically and track the file until the RCS registration is recorded and the Kbis extract is generated.
required_dossiers: Form M0 duly completed
Signed statuts and annexes
Attestation of publication issued by the JAL
Certificate of blocked share capital deposit
Registered office proof (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Gérant identity document and declaration of acceptance
Declaration of fitness and no legal incapacity
Regulated activity declaration (alcohol wholesale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond within the regulatory 15-day correction window to any incompleteness query; file supplementary documents electronically; if registration is refused, request a formal decision and re-submit after remediation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Administrative Completion: Kbis, SIREN/SIRET, URSSAF Affiliation and VAT Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Kbis extract); INSEE and DGFiP (national identifiers and VAT number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certified Kbis extract and verify all corporate data; confirm automatic allotment of SIREN, SIRET, and the intra-community French VAT number by DGFiP; verify URSSAF employer registration; open the definitive commercial bank account in the registered company name; retain all official extracts for licensing and customs procedures.
required_dossiers: Registration receipt from the Greffe
Kbis extract less than 3 months old
Final statuts stamped file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply for administrative rectification with the greffe or INSEE for any data mismatch; incorrect VAT numbers must be referred to DGFiP and re-issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Licence, Manager's Permit and Customs/Excise Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Préfecture de Paris – Bureau des débits de boissons et licences; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) – Direction Interrégionale des Douanes d'Île-de-France, Service des Alcools
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for the wholesale alcohol licence (licence de vente en gros) under Article L.3332-3 of the Public Health Code, attaching the Kbis, the gérant's validated permis d'exploitation certificate (accredited pre-licence training), the warehousing address and the company's AML/criminal record declarations. Simultaneously register the excise/activity file with DGDDI and, if untaxed alcohol is stored, apply for the bonded warehouse operator status with a suitable customs guarantee.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract after RCS registration
Manager's permis d'exploitation certificate
Application form for licence de vente en gros (Cerfa 11527*04)
Warehouse lease or storage agreement and layout plan
Criminal record extract and prior convictions declaration
DGDDI excise activity notice and category declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the prefecture opposes licensing on zoning or criminal-record grounds, file supplementary documents or change the registered operating site; if DGDDI queries excise data or guarantees, adjust the bonding guarantee or split bonded and non-bonded storage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Registration (ICPE Rubrique 1450) and Civil-Defence / Fire-Safety Clearance for the Warehousing Facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DREAL Île-de-France – Inspection des Installations Classées; Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS 75); CARSAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ascertain whether the maximum storage of high-proof baijiu (40–53% ABV) triggers the ICPE declaration threshold; if so, file the initial declaration (Cerfa 15272) under Rubrique 1450. Obtain SDIS clearance for fire compartmentation, sprinklers and evacuation; carry out workplace risk assessment and occupational health clearance with CARSAT; keep all certificates available for inspection.
required_dossiers: ICPE initial declaration form under Rubrique 1450
Maximum inventory statement (litres of 40–53% ABV alcohol)
Warehouse plans and fire-safety layout
Structural survey certificate from an approved bureau de contrôle
SDIS inspection certificate
CARSAT occupational prevention and risk assessment report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DREAL completeness requests within 30 days; implement additional fire-safety measures; modify the declaration thresholds by segmenting the warehouse or reducing peak inventory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture de Paris – Direction des Débits de Boissons et Licences; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) – Service des Alcools; DREAL Île-de-France for environmental and ICPE oversight
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence de Vente en Gros d'Alcool (Public Health Code, Articles L.3332-1 to L.3332-9) supplemented by the Manager's Permis d'Exploitation and, where bonded storage is used, the Agrément d'Entrepositaire Agréé issued by the DGDDI

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) Île-de-France – Inspection des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Régime de Déclaration (D) under ICPE Rubrique 1450 for storage of flammable alcoholic liquids above regulatory thresholds (typically > 5,000 L pure alcohol); no full environmental impact assessment (EIA) report required for pure wholesale distribution warehousing below 500 t of stored substances
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions for closed-bottle wholesale operations; sanitary wastewater discharged to municipal sewer per local arrêté; packaging waste compliance with Articles L.541-21 of the Environmental Code and EU Packaging Directive 94/62/EC; firewater retention and spill-containment basins are required by SDIS; damaged or spoiled stock disposed of under regulated waste handling codes

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS 75) covering compartmentation, exit routes, extinguishing systems and alarm; structural-load inspection certificate issued by an approved bureau de contrôle; CARSAT occupational risk assessment, workplace medical clearance and mandatory safety signage; compliance with ERP/warehouse classification of the building.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); taxpayer portal impots.gouv.fr; incorporation and registration portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique); non-resident corporate and VAT file: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), Paris.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Form the SARL via the Guichet Unique at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); INSEE automatically allocates SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits); local SIE opens the corporate tax file under the SIREN; intra-Community VAT number (FR + 2-digit control key + SIREN, 13 characters) is issued by the DGFiP after filing form P0 (n° 3310) at incorporation or on demand. Non-resident companies file an identification application with the SIEE, attaching certificate of existence, constitutional documents, power of attorney, proof of French permanent establishment, and VAT representative certificate where applicable; EU-resident applicants receive the VAT ID within days and third-country applicants within 2-3 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a commercial SARL is default taxable to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at the standard 25% rate (2025), reduced to 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of profit for SME SARLs with turnover under EUR 10 million; profits are taxed at entity level and no shareholder pass-through applies unless a valid election is made; head-office and export trading profits fall within French territorial scope under Article 209 I CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; statutory elections: (1) Article 239 bis AA CGI — a small SARL (turnover below EUR 10 million, qualifying shareholding and management condition) or family SARL may elect pass-through taxation at personal income tax (IR); (2) Article 223 A et seq. CGI — a 95% parent SARL may elect French tax consolidation (intégration fiscale); (3) anti-hybrid rules enacted by the 2019 Finance Act — no elective neutrality; deduction/inclusion mismatches with a US or Chinese shareholder are automatically disallowed.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French VAT), Articles 256 to 261 D CGI, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by DGFiP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise base thresholds for VAT exemption: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for sales of goods (tolerance ceiling EUR 93,500) and EUR 37,500 for services (tolerance EUR 41,400); the baijiu goods-export activity exceeding the ceiling is mandatorily VAT registered; non-resident traders have no exemption threshold and must register for any taxable French supply unless the customer is reverse-charge liable; exporters claiming Article 262-I zero-rating must hold a valid French VAT number and file periodic TVA returns to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing reform: B2B invoices must comply with the EN 16931 semantic model (Factur-X, UBL 2.1 or UN/CEFACT CII) and be transmitted to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF / Chorus Pro) through an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP); phased obligations run from 1 September 2026 (all VAT payers must receive; large enterprises must issue and transmit e-invoices and B2C e-reporting) to 1 September 2027 (all enterprises must issue); France applies data-driven clearance via certified PDP-PPF API interfaces without per-invoice digital stamping; penalties: EUR 15 per missing e-invoice (cap EUR 15,000 per year) and EUR 250 per missing e-reporting transmission (cap EUR 2,500 per year).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 262-I 1° CGI zero-rates exports of goods physically dispatched to a destination outside the European Union, with full input VAT deduction and refundable credit; eligibility requires the exporting SARL to invoice at 0%, hold the DAU customs export declaration in its own name, prove physical departure from the EU within 90 days from the date of supply, and document buyer identity, quantity and transport; services and commission directly connected to goods exported to non-EU destinations may also be zero-rated under Article 259-1° CGI; baijiu exports are simultaneously released from French alcohol excise duty (droits de consommation) under the duty-suspension regime of Article 302 D CGI, while domestic French sales remain taxable at 20%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration Unique d'Exportation, DAU) mit EX1 status via the DELTA customs clearance system
Bill of Lading or International Air Waybill evidencing physical EU exit and transfer of risk
Commercial invoice issued by the exporting French SARL at 0% TVA
Packing list and certificate of origin for the Chinese baijiu
Inward remittance certificate — SWIFT MT103 credit advice evidencing foreign currency receipt
Export sales contract or proforma invoice with Incoterms and pricing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Incomplete export evidence triggers retrospective recharacterization as a domestic taxable delivery with 20% VAT clawback on the full invoice value plus deduction reversal; penalties: 10% on wrongly zero-rated invoices (Article 1788 A CGI, minimum EUR 480 per infraction), 50% for fictitious invoicing (Article 1737 ter CGI), 80% for concealed activity and 100% for organized VAT fraud, plus 0.2% monthly late-payment interest; customs prosecution under the Code des douanes can impose fines of one to three times the value of undeclared goods and imprisonment up to 6 months (up to 2 years for alcohol export fraud schemes); DGFiP datamining cross-checks DAU records, transport documents and SWIFT receipts, and any FX repatriation delay beyond 180 days creates a presumption of non-genuine export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, as the French national central bank within the Eurosystem and under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange activity is principally governed by European Union law, French financial legislation, the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution for supervised financial institutions, the Autorité des marchés financiers for investment-services and market-conduct matters, and customs and statistical authorities for trade reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro. The euro is fully convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, customs, prudential, and financial-market controls. There is generally no French exchange-control approval for a SARL receiving foreign equity, shareholder loans, trade receipts, dividends, interest, royalties, or sale proceeds. Profit remittances are not subject to a statutory foreign-exchange quota, but require corporate authorization, legally distributable profits where applicable, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing support for related-party payments, beneficial-owner verification, and evidence of the underlying transaction. Non-EU payments may be subject to bank transaction screening, sanctions screening, correspondent-bank requirements, and regulatory or statistical reporting. Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, dual-use goods, or unusual trade routes may be blocked or require enhanced due diligence. Dividend distributions require approved financial statements, satisfaction of French legal-reserve requirements, solvency and corporate-law conditions, and withholding-tax and treaty analysis. Interest on shareholder loans requires arm's-length pricing, thin-capitalization and interest-limitation analysis, beneficial-ownership review, and applicable withholding-tax documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory obligation requiring exporters to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into euros. The SARL may retain eligible foreign-currency balances with a regulated bank, subject to the bank's account terms and applicable payment, sanctions, AML, accounting, tax, and reporting rules. Export transactions must still be supported by commercial invoices, transport and customs records, proof of delivery where relevant, and accurate accounting. For exports outside the European Union, customs declarations and applicable French and European Union trade-statistics obligations must be satisfied. Alcohol exports may additionally require excise, customs, and movement-control documentation, including applicable EMCS procedures. Any bank-specific conversion, balance, or repatriation requirement is contractual rather than a general French exchange-control rule.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ordinary EUR collections and payments, but not a complete substitute for a French relationship bank. An EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, safeguarding, SEPA transfers, cards, and selected foreign-currency services, subject to its authorization perimeter, passporting status, safeguarding model, limits, and risk policy. An EMI account is not automatically a bank deposit account and normally does not provide statutory SARL capital-deposit certification unless the provider is legally authorized and willing to perform that service. Access to cash services, French bank drafts, sophisticated commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, borrowing, overdrafts, guarantees, and certain trade-finance products may be unavailable. Offshore digital EMIs without appropriate European Union authorization, passporting, or a regulated European payment partner should not be used for core operating flows. The SARL must maintain documentary evidence of source of funds, beneficial ownership, business purpose, counterparties, expected volumes, jurisdictions, and alcohol-trade compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically appear at a branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or reliable electronic identification, corporate-registry evidence, video identification, electronic signatures, and certified documents. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, wet-ink documents, a local authorized signatory, notarized or apostilled foreign documents, or a face-to-face interview based on risk, ownership complexity, non-resident management, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual payment corridors, or inability to verify identity electronically. A SARL formation capital deposit and issuance of the certificate of deposit are subject to the selected bank's procedure and may be completed remotely only if that bank accepts the relevant incorporation and identity-verification process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, layered ownership, or inability to identify natural persons controlling more than the applicable French beneficial-owner threshold or otherwise exercising control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the French commercial register or equivalent incorporation records; articles of association; ownership chart to natural-person level; beneficial-owner declaration filed with the competent French register where required; passports and proof of address for shareholders, managers, directors, and beneficial owners; shareholder agreements; powers of attorney; and a signed ownership and control certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or manager, foreign corporate parent, or documents issued in a jurisdiction requiring enhanced verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and good standing for each foreign entity; constitutional documents; board resolutions; certified translations where required; apostille or legalization where required; tax-identification evidence; identity and address evidence for relevant individuals; group organization chart; explanation of the French operating rationale; and documented authority of each signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-proof alcohol distribution, potential excise exposure, restricted-market sales, or incomplete licensing and customs profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; product specifications and alcohol percentages; supplier and customer list; applicable French alcohol wholesaler, storage, excise, customs, and food-safety registrations or permits; EORI evidence; customs procedures; EMCS arrangements where applicable; warehouse and logistics contracts; import and export flow chart; sanctions and export-control screening policy; and proof that counterparties are licensed and commercially legitimate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: China-related payment flows, Chinese baijiu supply chain, unusual intermediaries, third-party payments, or corridors involving elevated sanctions or AML risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed purchase and sales contracts; invoices; bills of lading; packing lists; customs declarations; certificates of origin; proof of delivery; beneficial-owner information for counterparties; bank-account ownership confirmations; explanation of every intermediary; payment-routing matrix; sanctions-screening records; anti-bribery policy; and written prohibition of unexplained third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected turnover, transaction frequency, or cash activity inconsistent with the stated low-risk profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve- to twenty-four-month cash-flow forecast; monthly transaction-volume and value estimates; currency matrix; expected countries and counterparties; source-and-use-of-funds schedule; opening balance evidence; financing documents; management accounts; tax-registration evidence; and reconciliation controls demonstrating separation of customer receipts, supplier payments, taxes, payroll, and shareholder funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive operations, unexplained cash deposits, or use of personal accounts for corporate transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written cash-minimization policy; prohibition on personal accounts; approved corporate payment policy; cash-register and inventory controls; source-of-cash evidence where unavoidable; daily reconciliation procedures; accountant or auditor confirmation; and documented escalation rules for unusual transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative media, sanctions exposure, politically exposed persons, criminal-history concerns, or adverse regulatory information affecting a shareholder, manager, supplier, customer, or intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions and PEP screening reports; identity clarification; legal opinions or court dispositions where relevant; beneficial-owner declarations; compliance certifications; enhanced due-diligence memorandum; counterparty risk assessment; and documented decision to reject or restrict high-risk relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for unexplained foreign-currency conversions, rapid in-and-out transfers, circular flows, or payments lacking a credible commercial purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-purpose register; underlying contracts and invoices; customs and shipping records; board or management approvals; intercompany pricing support; bank statements; reconciliation to the general ledger; documented treasury policy; and evidence that conversion amounts correspond to genuine trade, financing, tax, or hedging requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax, VAT, customs, or alcohol-compliance registrations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax and VAT registration evidence; intra-Community VAT number where applicable; EORI number; customs broker appointment; excise registrations or authorizations where applicable; warehouse and transport documentation; tax-compliance calendar; accountant engagement letter; and copies of filed returns or a documented pre-trading explanation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity capital through the designated French capital-deposit account before SARL registration, using a traceable transfer from the subscriber's account and identifying the payer as the shareholder or subscribing entity. Provide the bank with the draft articles, subscription schedule, shareholder resolution or subscription instrument, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner information, and incorporation documents. After registration, route additional equity through the French corporate EUR account with a board or shareholder resolution and accounting classification as share capital, share premium, or another legally supported contribution. Route shareholder loans under a signed loan agreement specifying principal, currency, maturity, interest, repayment terms, subordination if applicable, and transfer-pricing support. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border transfer, ordinarily using ISO 20022 payment messages and legacy MT103 where supported, for non-SEPA or correspondent-bank flows. Include the correct IBAN, BIC, legal entity name, registered address, payment purpose, invoice or agreement reference, and any bank-requested purpose code. Do not describe a capital contribution as a trade payment or use third-party settlement without documented legal and commercial justification. Banks may request source-of-wealth, source-of-funds, tax-residence, sanctions, and beneficial-owner evidence before crediting funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA transfers for eligible EUR supplier payments and regulated-bank SWIFT transfers for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. A SWIFT MT103 may be used where supported, although ISO 20022 cross-border payment messages are increasingly standard. For documentary trade, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit subject to UCP 600, preferably confirmed where country or bank risk warrants confirmation. Define beneficiary, amount, currency, expiry, latest shipment date, presentation period, partial-shipment and transshipment rules, Incoterms, required commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin, insurance document, customs evidence, and any product or excise certificate. Use documentary collections under URC 522 where the risk profile is acceptable. Ensure the ordering party, beneficiary, goods description, countries, vessels, banks, and intermediaries pass sanctions and export-control screening. Reconcile each payment to the purchase order, invoice, shipping record, customs declaration, and general ledger. For imported or exported spirits, verify customs valuation, tariff classification, excise treatment, VAT treatment, origin claims, transport documentation, and any alcohol-specific movement-control requirements before settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forwards with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm, used to hedge documented forecast or committed trade exposures and supported by an approved treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or markets where physical delivery is restricted, subject to counterparty authorization, applicable MiFID II, EMIR, reporting, collateral, suitability, and documentation requirements.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing recurring funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent master documentation, EMIR requirements, collateral terms, valuation controls, and counterparty-credit limits.

Plain-vanilla FX options, collars, and option-based hedges may be available for genuine commercial exposures, subject to appropriateness, cost, accounting, documentation, and bank-risk controls; speculative or disproportionate structures should be prohibited.

Spot foreign-exchange conversion through a regulated bank or authorized payment provider for settlement and liquidity purposes. Because France uses the euro, hedging is principally relevant to CNY, USD, GBP, and other non-euro exposures rather than domestic EUR cash flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be convened within 6 months after financial year-end; accounts must be deposited within 3 months after AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €1,500; repeated non-filing may trigger dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update required within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding; annual verification mandated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and potential company strike-off for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if turnover exceeds €800,000, balance sheet total exceeds €400,000 or average headcount exceeds 50 employees; small SARL otherwise exempt
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan Comptable Général - PCG)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review and update of Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs required; shareholding transfers must be notified to the company and Greffe within 1 month if they alter control or exceed ownership thresholds

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €0 - €4,000 (exempt for qualifying small SARL; required audit fees otherwise)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT 25%; reduced 15% rate for taxable profits up to EUR 42,500 where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 10m; tax credits for qualifying R&D (CIR 30%) and innovation (CII 20%); parent-subsidiary regime exempts qualifying intra-group dividend income and reduces the effective rate if no foreign counterpart tax sheltering is present.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Liasse fiscale form no. 2065 with schedules 2058-A to 2058-X; electronically filed through the French tax portal at impots.gouv.fr via the EDIF/GESTA filaire system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual tax return is due by the second working day after 1 May of the following year; for off-calendar-year accounting periods, the return is generally due within 60 days of the fiscal year-end. Corporate tax instalments are due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: SIREN, SIRET, legal form, registered concerned address, tax residence indicator, non-resident PE indicator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-French resident SARL without a French permanent establishment marks the relevant foreign-resident box; if a French PE exists, provide the PE’s French address and identify the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year closing date, reporting currency, elected consolidation or tax-integration regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert all amounts to EUR at the EUR/CNY ECB fixing rate on the closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue: wholesale and export sales of Chinese baijiu, net of discounts and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French-source revenue attributable to a French PE or distribution activity is reportable by a non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases of baijiu inventory and change in inventory; cost of goods sold for customs-cleared export cargo.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base inventory valuation on FIFO or weighted-average cost under French GAAP; retain customs clearance documents for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet entries: trade receivables, intercompany loans, bank balances, goodwill and negative goodwill.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany loans from the Chinese parent or affiliates must be documented by a written agreement with arm’s length interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains or ordinary profits derived from disposal of assets, distribution rights, trademarks or export licences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capital gains from the disposal of French PE assets are taxable at the standard 25% CIT rate unless a treaty override applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after expenses, loss carryforwards and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses generated by a French branch/PE can only offset its own French-source profits; head-office losses are not deductible in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reclaimed, foreign tax credits, and avoir fiscal where permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Chinese tax residency certificates and Form 5000/5001 series to claim DTA reduced withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 5% moratory increase (rising to 10% after a formal request) plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.40%; deliberate understatement adds a 40% administrative penalty and abuse-of-law transactions an 80% penalty; non-electronic filing of large groups can add a penalty of 0.2% of gross revenue.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% of gross dividends paid by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders unless reduced by a tax treaty or excluded under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive after a 2-year minimum holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide the French paying agent or the SARL with a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the Chinese or other DTA tax authority, together with a Form 5000/5001 declaration confirming beneficial ownership, shareholding percentage and holding period. The reduced withholding is applied only if the documentation is received before payment; otherwise the excess may be reclaimed by filing a réclamation within the statutory limitation period (31 December of the second year following the distribution).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents, trademarks, software and similar IP paid by a French SARL to non-residents are subject to a domestic withholding rate of 33.33%, reduced to 10% under the France-China DTA. Interest payments by a French company to foreign lenders are generally exempt from French withholding tax under domestic provisions; if a withholding is assessable, the France-China DTA sets a 10% ceiling for interest and the EU Interest-Royalties Directive may relieve qualifying affiliated residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000: a French group or standalone SARL with annual consolidated turnover or total assets exceeding EUR 400m is required to prepare and file the Local File and Master File under French TP documentation obligations; all taxpayers are nonetheless expected to retain basic TP adjustment documentation adequate for audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime like offshore standard ESR, but economic substance remains decisive in determining corporate tax residency under Article 209, in applying the French GAAR (abus de droit and Loi de régulation sociale), and in obtaining treaty benefits under BEPS Action 6; a Chattel and network substance review is required for all SARL shareholders and beneficial owners to avoid sham declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of overseas baijiu export revenue, falsification of invoices, or under-declaration of French-source profits through unaccounted SWIFT wires or letters of credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud (fraude fiscale) is punishable by up to 5 years’ imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated cases carry 10 years and EUR 4.5m; administrative reassessment applies an 80% penalty for intentional concealment plus 0.40% monthly interest and forfeiture of deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be personally ordered to pay the totality of tax debts, interest and penalties; courts can issue travel bans, prohibit management activity, order restitution of company assets, and impose civil restitution when the company is insolvent or the veil-piercing conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SARL without real staff, premises or operating activity, while directing baijiu procurement and sales from China and using DTA provisions to drain French tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the French anti-abuse provision (80% penalty under Article 1729 b), denial of treaty benefits and extraterritorial reattribution of profits; the tax administration can recharacterise the SARL as a sham and tax its entire profit at 25% in the hands of the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers are jointly and severally liable for tax and penalties; a ‘gestion de fait’ finding can make them personally responsible for 100% of the tax liability; significant fraud charges may result in arrest guarantees and prohibition from running French entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially inflating the cost of Chinese baijiu imports from a related supplier, paying non-sensical fees to a related Hong Kong or Singapore service company, or shifting all European profit out of France via an unapproved TNMM mark-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment with reimbursed tax, 40% penalty for severe lack of documentation or false information under Article 1735-B, 80% penalty for sham price manipulation, and monthly late-payment interest of 0.40%; total sanctions may exceed 100% of the corrected tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who signed false transfer pricing certificates can be held personally liable for penalty amounts; criminal tax fraud proceedings can lead to imprisonment and confiscation of personal assets when the pricing is knowingly fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and AML Deficiency in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting trade payment via SWIFT wires or L/Cs without performing KYC/CDD on the Chinese supplier and ultimate beneficial owners, using third-party payment passes or transacting through accounts of shell companies in sanctioned jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French Monetary and Financial Code sanctions include administrative fines up to EUR 1m or 1% of cleared transactions for failing CDD/AML controls, criminal prosecution for laundering (up to 10 years’ imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine) and confiscation of funds/inventory related to the laundering scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Banking and AML supervisors may prohibit the manager from exercising managerial functions for up to 10 years; criminal courts may impose personal fines, disgorge profits, and seize personal bank accounts where the SARL director knowingly implements sham payment structures and receives commission on concealed exports.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Breach of Excise and Alcohol Licensing Regulations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling or distributing Chinese baijiu through EU-bound cargo without registration for the French excise tax (Droit de consommation), without VAT valuation for alcohol, or without the obligatory ADE/AE-FA e-commerce customs declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of EUR 750 per missing declaration; excise duty at the rate applicable per hectolitre of pure alcohol (approximately EUR 1,740 per hlP); confiscation of seized inventory; surcharge and interest for late reporting, and prohibition of the activity in the case of repeat violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is personally liable for penalties when he/she personally authorised the undeclared importation; under customs legislation, the registered customs representative and the managing director may be jointly liable and subject to seizure of personal property if the company has no substantial assets to satisfy the excise penalty.
